items.title: Pakistan's Sharif urges Trump to extend Iran deadline two weeks

featured_image.name: Trump extends deadline for Iran to reopen oil route or face ... - PBS

items.description:
Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday called on President Donald Trump to extend his deadline for Iran by two weeks, issuing a public plea just hours before Trump's 8 p.m. Eastern time ultimatum that has threatened devastating strikes on Iranian power plants and bridges.

"I earnestly request President Trump to extend the deadline for two weeks," Sharif wrote in a message posted on X, according to The Wall Street Journal. He also called on Tehran to temporarily reopen the Strait of Hormuz for the same two-week period "as a sign of goodwill," and urged all warring parties to observe a ceasefire across all fronts to allow diplomacy to produce a lasting resolution.[1][2]

items.title: Kuwait orders residents indoors as Trump's Iran deadline looms

featured_image.name: Kuwait Is Set to Allow Banks to Offer Mortgages for the First Time

items.description: Kuwait's Ministry of Interior on Tuesday urged all citizens and residents to stay home and avoid going outdoors from midnight to 6:00 a.m. on Wednesday, April 8, citing precautionary security measures as regional tensions reach a critical juncture. The directive, described as a "precautionary measure," comes as President Donald Trump's 8 p.m. Eastern deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz approaches Tuesday evening, with the president warning of devastating strikes on Iranian infrastructure if no deal is reached.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Leaked transcript shows Orbán offered to serve Putin

featured_image.name: Ukraine war: Hungary's PM Viktor Orban meets Putin in Moscow

items.description:
Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán told Russian President Vladimir Putin he was ready to assist him "in any way" during a phone call last October, according to a Hungarian government transcript reviewed by Bloomberg and published on Monday.[1][2]

"Yesterday our friendship rose to such a high level that I can help in any way," Orbán told Putin during the October 17, 2025, conversation, according to the transcript. "In any matter where I can be of assistance, I am at your service."[2][1]

To illustrate his readiness to serve, Orbán referenced a well-known Hungarian children's tale in which a mouse rescues a lion from a trap after the lion had previously spared the mouse's life.[2]

items.title: Iran severs all diplomatic channels with US ahead of Trump's Hormuz deadline

featured_image.name: Iran war: What is happening on day 39 of US-Israeli attacks?

items.description:
Iran on Tuesday shut down all diplomatic and indirect communication channels with the United States, according to the state-run Tehran Times, in a dramatic escalation that came just hours before President Donald Trump's self-imposed deadline for Tehran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The move effectively closes off avenues for last-minute negotiations as the six-week-old war enters one of its most dangerous phases.[1][2]

"Iran has closed all diplomatic and indirect channels of communication with the United States. Any and all message exchanges have also been suspended," the Tehran Times reported. The Wall Street Journal, citing a Middle Eastern official, reported that the cutoff of direct diplomacy was intended to signal Tehran's disapproval of Trump's threats, though it noted that some mediated discussions may still be ongoing.[3][4][1]

items.title: UK bars Ye from entering country, Wireless Festival canceled

featured_image.name: Ministers reviewing Kanye West's permission to enter UK

items.description:
The British government on Tuesday denied Ye, the rapper formerly known as Kanye West, permission to enter the United Kingdom, prompting the immediate cancellation of this year's Wireless Festival in London. The Home Office rejected Ye's application for an Electronic Travel Authorisation on the grounds that his presence would not be "conducive to the public good," according to the BBC.[1][2]

Ye had been announced as the sole headliner for the three-day Wireless Festival, scheduled for July 10-12 in Finsbury Park, where he was expected to perform before roughly 150,000 attendees. Festival Republic, the event's organizer, confirmed the cancellation and said refunds would be issued to all ticket holders.[3][2][4]
